svg.title: Copper Scroll entry 24: the tomb in the Wadi of the Vault
svg.text: Entry 24 (V 12–14) — the tomb in the Wadi of the Vault
Schematic plan, north up, not to scale. One arrangement the text allows; the text gives no bearing for the route and no size for the tomb.
Project reading: a tomb in the wadi, on the Jericho–Secacah approach
“From Jericho” is read by Milik, Puech, Beyer and Lefkovits; the route is a
general approach to test, not a journey continued from entry 23.
Wadi of the Vault · נחל הכפא
on the north bank: Puech's placement
Allegro read no Jericho and no route (Puech 2015 p. 59
n. 232): the deposit goes by the tomb's eastern entrance.
No approach from Jericho: the wadi alone locates the tomb.
Readings that leave the plan unchanged
the letters agree; “rock” or “cavern” is disputed (the
קבר is not disputed; the tomb is itself the hiding place
“from Jericho” is “certain” for Puech; the files test it
“In the tomb that is in the Wadi of the Vault, on the way from Jericho to Secacah, dig seven cubits:
The route runs north to south as the atlas places Jericho and Secacah; the text gives no bearing. The
tomb is on the north bank (Puech); seven cubits is a depth.
Atlas: best-supported, low. Wadi Kuteif preferred (low), between Jericho and Qumran (Milik; Puech
follows). The placement rests mainly on the route.
SWP p. 220 and Milik D12 describe one rock-cut, stepped underground chamber in Wadi Kuteif, undated;
it is not taken as the entry's tomb (phase5_assessments.csv).
